To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new protein D was identified, cloned, characterized, and found to be an important regulator of SP-B expression.
a new DNA binding factor, protein D, is identified, cloned and sequenced, and that it increases SP-B promoter activity in response to glucorticoids.
the glucocorticoid-responsive protein D is a new member of the bzip family of DNA binding proteins and that it stimulates SP-B promoter activity in response to glucorticoids.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of a novel glucocorticoid-responsive protein that is capable of enhancing glucocorticoid-induced SP-B promoter activity in a cell line derived from type II alveol
the identification and characterization of proteins that bind the promoter region of the SP-B gene.
the mechanisms of glucocorticoid regulation of the surfactant gene SP-B, and the results suggest that a new DNA binding transcription factor, protein D, is involved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein D is a new DNA-binding protein of the bzip type that is capable of increasing the activity of the surfactant protein B promoter when it is stimulated by glucocorticoids.
protein D is a new DNA-binding protein that binds a site in the promoter of SP-B and enhances the glucocorticoid-induced activation of SP-B gene transcription.
the protein D is a new DNA-binding protein, whose carboxyl-terminal domain contains a modified basic region-leucine zipper-like motif.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified and characterized a new DNA binding transcription factor that is a glucocorticoid responsive element (GRE) binding protein.
glucocorticoid hormones stimulate SP-B expression by binding to glucocorticoids receptors (GR).
we cloned and characterized a novel protein that binds the promoter of a surfactant protein gene and that it confers glucocorticoid response to this promoter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SP-B promoter is a good model for glucocorticoid action in the lung.
we have identified a new glucocorticoid-responsive gene activator, which we call protein D.
we identified a new DNA-binding protein that binds to the SP-B promoter at an NF1 element and that confers glucocorticoid sensitivity to this promoter.
